text:
anya: quick heads-up — onboarding a new mpt-7b-chat variant failed during hf2rdw-convert, getting a safetensors shard index mismatch error.
anya: command i ran: `hf2rdw-convert --model hf://user/mpt-7b-chat --out /tmp/rdw-mpt --quant q4_0`
anya: log snippet:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/usr/local/bin/hf2rdw-convert\", line 312, in <module>
    write_shard(shard_idx, weights)
IndexError: requested shard 3 but safetensors.index.json only lists shards [0,1]
```
leo: can you paste the full safetensors.index.json from the hub snapshot? curious if the index file itself references different filenames or a different ordering.
anya: here it is (trimmed): `{"weight_000.safetensors": 0, "weight_001.safetensors": 1}` but the archive actually contains `weight_000.safetensors, weight_001.safetensors, weight_002.safetensors` on disk.
rebecca: hmm that smells like a revision-pin / upload race — some hubs rewrite the index when a push partially finishes. did you pin a revision or pass `--revision`?
sam: also worth noting: our quantizer step `rename_keys_v2` can create new weight names (adds `_q` suffix) which shifts expected shard assignment if the converter relies on deterministic iteration order.
ci-bot: convert-job/rdw-hf2rdw-843 FAILED (exit 1) — see logs https://ci.redwood.ai/job/843
leo: probable root cause: converter used os.listdir() when building the index, which is non-deterministic across platforms. if the converter maps weights -> shard index by that arbitrary order then writing will mismatch the safetensors.index.json produced by the uploader. quick fix: sort filenames before assigning indices and write index with the same canonical order.
anya: tested locally with a patched converter that sorts names alphabetically; conversion completes without the IndexError. however, after load there's still a mismatch in chat behavior — some system special tokens are missing from tokenizers.json.
rebecca: token mapping issue is separate: many HF chat templates rely on custom added tokens like `<|system|>` and legacy `added_tokens` fields. our convert step currently drops unknown legacy token entries. quick workaround: run `python -c \"from tokenizers import AddedToken; ...\"` to transplant `added_tokens` into new `tokenizer.json`, or use `--preserve-added-tokens` flag (i pushed a small patch to accept that flag).
sam: for the safetensors path, longer-term we should validate the index after writing and, on mismatch, attempt a fallback: (1) read safetensors.index.json from hub and map by filename, (2) download any missing shard files by name instead of by index, (3) emit a warning and continue. this avoids brittle behavior when authors repin or uploads complete out-of-order.
anya: thanks — can someone open an issue and a quick PR? i'll run regression evals once a patch lands. we need to ensure quantized weights produce no perplexity regression.
leo: opened https://github.com/redwood/infer/issues/4567 — title: "hf2rdw-convert: non-deterministic shard ordering + dropped added_tokens -> conversion failures". labels: eng/bug, priority/p1, area/ingestion.
rebecca: i'll submit the `--preserve-added-tokens` flag PR and add a mapping table for common chat template tokens (system, user, assistant).
sam: i'll add a unit test that simulates a hub snapshot with mismatched index vs files and assert the fallback path downloads by filename. also schedule canary rollout to Dedicated so we don't break customer imports.
ci-bot: PR #789 merged into main by rebecca — CI green.
rebecca: :white_check_mark: merged and released in 0.9.3-alpha; added notes to the import docs about revision pinning and quantizer key renames.
sam: after patch, please run the evals: compare perplexity and a 200-example chat eval set (we care about instruction-following regressions). if q4_0 quant produced >2% quality regression, rollback quant and try q5 or tweak per-channel quant params.
anya: will do. thanks all for the rapid turnaround — filing postmortem notes in the onboarding doc.
